cards.text: After this, Samuel calls the people together to the LORD at Mizpah. Samuel is Israel's prophet, and he's got a message for the whole crowd. It comes straight from the LORD, the God of Israel.

cards.question: The LORD's message to Israel at Mizpah starts with a reminder. What does He say He did for them?

answers.text: Brought them up out of Egypt
Gave them a king long ago
Built them a city at Mizpah

cards.text: Then Samuel turns it around: today, he says, they have rejected their God, who saves them from all their troubles and afflictions. They've told Him, “No, set a king over us.”

cards.question: So Samuel tells Israel to present themselves before the LORD. They'll come forward by their tribes and ___.

cards.text: So all the tribes of Israel come forward. I know this feeling, friend: YEARS in a junk drawer, holding my breath every time it opened to see who was getting picked.

cards.question: All the tribes of Israel come forward before the LORD. Which tribe is selected?
Next the tribe of Benjamin comes forward clan by clan, and the clan of Matri is selected. Then one man is selected. Who is it?

cards.text: Saul son of Kish is the pick! A WHOLE nation narrowed down to ONE man, they go to get him, and... NOBODY can find him.

cards.question: They inquire of the LORD again, “Has the man come here yet?” The LORD replies that Saul has ___ himself among the baggage.
They run and bring Saul out. When he stands among the people, he's a head taller than any of them.

cards.text: Then Samuel says to all the people, “Do you see the one the LORD has chosen? There is no one like him among all the people.” That is a BIG introduction for a man they just pulled out of the luggage.

cards.question: Samuel presents Saul as the one the LORD has chosen. All the people shout: long live the ___!

cards.text: Then Samuel explains the rights of kingship to the people. I bet the new king is still brushing baggage dust off his shoulders.

cards.question: Samuel explains the rights of kingship to the people, but he never writes them down.

cards.text: Samuel writes them on a scroll and lays it up before the LORD. Then he sends all the people away, each to his own home.

cards.question: Saul heads to his home in Gibeah too. Who goes with him?

answers.text: Men of valor God had touched

cards.text: But not everybody's on board. Some worthless men say, “How can this man save us?”

cards.question: Those worthless men despise Saul and bring him no gifts. How does Saul respond?

answers.text: He calls them out in public

cards.text: Not one word from the new king, and I'm impressed, because say ONE thing about my mustache and I've got a twenty-minute speech ready. But that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this king's story is far from over.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the unseen wording “tribes and clans.” Nothing in cards 1–3 gives the baker a basis for reasoning out “clans,” so this becomes a guess at the next word of the line rather than a test of meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Too many choices depend on discovering a fact rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. Cards 2, 6, 10, 14, 16 and 18 provide no earlier-card basis for working out the Exodus reminder, Benjamin, Saul's height, the writing of the scroll, Saul's companions or Saul's silence. That makes six of the ten choice cards discovery questions, so most choices are not informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
